candidate: 國立屏東科技大學第二餐廳：主餐廳與相連東服務翼
decision: Formal complete architectural plans/elevations/sections, two completed-building ground photographs and independent orthophoto together close the principal exterior topology. Permitted as a source-bound exterior approximation, not a complete 2026/as-built survey.

review_history.new_evidence_resolving_gap: Personally inspected the complete NLSC assembly AND each of its four original tiles. These show the square four-hip principal roof/central square rooflight and the attached east service wing with three red roof strips around a central gray roof region, matching the drawn plan relationships. The earlier roof/wing main-topology gap is resolved, not silently ignored.

identity: Old museum A1-1 title says 國立屏東農業專科學校 學生餐廳 新建工程. Old #8 existing dining hall in north dormitories maps to modern #66 第一餐廳. Old application #32 beside the comprehensive teaching building and sports field maps to modern #69 第二餐廳 beside #68 綜合大樓/#63 運動場.
The drawing site is the second refectory location. Neither similarity to the first refectory interior nor assumed construction-year equivalence is used to establish identity.

Original title dates 78.6/revision79.8 are design/revision evidence; not an assertion of construction in1989/1990. Official history reported separately by coordinator gives second refectory March1997 completion. This reviewer has not independently re-extracted that HTML date.
required_geometry: Principal hall has nominal39.7m square outer roof plan, four hip/sloping red roof faces, and a central square rooflight. Avoid a plain gable or a flat full roof. Dimensions are original design dimensions, not field measurements.

The floor/peripheral circulation is not a filled square box: corner portions are chamfered, there are recessed wall/window lines behind the visible perimeter columns/beams, and raised entrance landings with stairs. West main entrance is central; north/south stair entrances differ in position, not a forced fourfold copy.

The main floor is raised over a partial basement shown by section/basement-window strips. Preserve the visible raised plinth and steps; buried basement interior may be omitted with disclosure, not exposed as a fictitious full open ground floor.

East lower service wing is attached by the narrow lower connecting zone and has three pitched roof strips: north/south shorter strips plus the long east strip. Their slopes descend toward the three outer edges, with the inner margins higher. Do not turn it into a second matching four-hip hall.

Central service-wing white/gray rectangle is NOT a courtyard open to the ground. The1F plan locates kitchen below; A4-1 longitudinal section has a horizontal roof/slab line above the kitchen with higher surrounding window/inner roof edges, and A2-3 references W9/W10/W11. Retain a covered central gray roof region and high surrounding side-window/roof relationships; avoid an invented open hole or unqualified raised all-glass skylight.

Main square rooflight appears as a very shallow four-sided cap with triangular tonal regions in the orthophoto. Design drawings show a curb and individual small cover/glazing shapes. A coarse low four-sided cap/rooflight is defensible; exact16modules, glazing pattern, or date of a possible replacement is not established.

Four different elevations and the partial-basement/roof sections may supply features obscured in photographs. They remain original design evidence, not proof that every existing door/window or rail is unchanged.
photo_comparison: mobile01-00 clearly names第二餐廳 and shows the central raised stair/landing, rectangular gray/white tile-column frame, recessed dark glazing, and red sloping roof above.

mobile01-01 supplies an offset stair/peripheral entrance and the raised low wall/basement opening relationship; its storefront/window arrangement is visible but not a license to mirror every elevation.

NLSC shows the major main/service roof shape without a competing unknown wing at the core. It resolves the earlier strongest design-versus-built roof concern, not rear-facade individual window detail.
scope_and_uncertainty: Include the complete original main dining hall plus its attached east service wing and essential visible access/plinth interfaces. Exclude neighboring comprehensive building, sports ground, detached campus buildings and landscaping.

At north/south yard areas outside the service wing, orthophoto has several pale rectangular objects/coverings. Their exact status as equipment, later small shelters, or additions is unresolved. Do not invent them as rooms, or assert that the original yards are entirely empty today. Explicitly omit later yard/equipment microstructures from this original-building exterior reconstruction.
Orthophoto watermark NLSC2024 is a copyright/product mark, not verified acquisition date. No2024/2026 present-condition claim.

Two ground-photo original capture dates are unknown here; image metadata lists no EXIF Original. Fine tile rows, window grids, exact rail/stair counts, rooflight framing, equipment and tiny roof details are approximate or omitted.
No interior restaurant furnishings, underground systems, kitchen equipment or physical-print reliability is promised.

Main hall and low service-wing roofs are now evidenced; absence of every rear-face close-up is not itself a remaining main-topology blocker when the formal complete drawings and observed principal roof/entry match are bounded as above.
